analysis:
This PR changes documentation only, in docs/provider/attestation.md and docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The attestation.md edits (head lines 17-20, 22-31, 107-117) describe App Attest control handling while model loading is suspended, official-build registration, and an endpoint-resumption challenge that reuses an in-memory key. They say these are not authorization and not enabled in production, and that the coordinator verdict remains authoritative. This is consistent with TB-011 and T-052..T-058. No regressions were found. I could not verify the code behind these claims.

The cli-reference.md edits add two behaviors.

1. A hidden `--native-serve-qualification-v1` diagnostic entry (head lines ~43-52). It is gated by an env var, a signed release app, 127.0.0.1 transport and owner-only inputs. It bypasses Start/APNs/daemon replacement. The next pass should check that the implementation enforces these gates and does not become a way to bypass serving authorization.

2. `logout` now stops the provider and revokes the token via POST /v1/device/revoke (head lines ~438-465). It sends the raw bearer token and follows no redirects. The docs do not state a TLS or origin requirement for the coordinator URL, which is taken from provider state or config (finding above). Revocation is best-effort, and local deletion proceeds if remote revocation fails.

The coordinator endpoint and the Swift implementation (ProviderLogout.swift, LogoutCommand.swift) were not supplied.

findings.detail: The new logout flow (documented only; the Swift code was not provided) captures the coordinator from the running provider's state, including a `start --coordinator` override. If there is no live snapshot, it falls back to the config file. After shutdown it sends the raw saved provider token as `Authorization: Bearer` to `POST /v1/device/revoke` at that coordinator. The docs say it uses a 10s timeout and follows no redirects. They do not say it requires `https`, or that it derives the HTTP origin from the `wss://` URL in the same way as the provider connection. A plaintext or attacker-chosen coordinator value in the override, state file or config would leak the long-lived provider token (A-008) during a routine logout. Because logout is meant to invalidate the credential, a leak at that point is especially unwelcome. The threat model has no entry for this new token-transmission path. Fix: enforce TLS and the same coordinator origin and allow-list as the provider WebSocket, refuse non-https URLs, and add this path to the TB-002/A-008 analysis.
findings.title: Logout sends the raw provider bearer token to a coordinator URL taken from local state, with no stated scheme or host check
